page: Microsoft Azure FX48-24mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1008.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2835 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2339.0 and a text processing score of 2938.0, both placing in the top 10%. Single-threaded compression and decompression are also strong, with gzip compression reaching 34.71 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.24 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall into the average tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 41633.42 and a large-block memory read bandwidth of 186.82 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated tile and integer operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX48-24mds_v2 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, balancing a massive memory footprint with high-frequency single-core execution. The presence of fast local NVMe SSD storage and strong single-thread performance makes this server highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, heavy text processing pipelines, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory capacity without requiring a massive virtual CPU count.
